in_arabic.name: دستگیر
in_arabic.meaning: الله کی مدد کرنے والا، دستگیر کرنے والا، قدرت رکھنے والا
in_arabic.long_meaning: دستگیر ایک ایسا نام ہے جو اللہ کی قدرت اور مدد کو ظاہر کرتا ہے۔ یہ نام عربی زبان کے دو الفاظ 'دست' اور 'گیر' سے بنا ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے ہاتھ اور پکڑنا۔ یہ نام اسلامی تقویم میں ایک اہم مقام رکھتا ہے، کیونکہ یہ اللہ کی قدرت اور انسانوں کی اس کے ساتھ وابستگی کو یاد دلاتا ہے۔

in_english.name: Dastgir
in_english.meaning: One who helps, empowers, or supports with their hand
in_english.long_meaning: The name Dastgir originates from Arabic roots, specifically from 'dast' meaning hand and 'gir' meaning to hold or grasp. It signifies one who provides assistance, support, or empowerment. In Islamic tradition, this name reflects the divine attribute of being powerful and supportive. It also alludes to the human relationship with the divine, emphasizing reliance on God's guidance and strength. Historically, Dastgir has been used across various Muslim cultures, symbolizing the virtues of compassion, protection, and divine providence.

historical_references.reference: Al-Dastgir bin Abdul Rahman Al-Khuza'i: A prominent Shia scholar and a vizier of the Buyid dynasty of Iraq (932-1062 CE). He was a close advisor to the Buyid emir al-Mu'tadid Billah (r. 945-978 CE) and played a significant role in the religious, cultural and political spheres of the Buyid state. His works include commentaries on the Quran and traditions of the Prophet Muhammad, and he is known for his contributions to the development of Shia jurisprudence.

Mir Sayyid Ali Hamadani (also known as Shah-i-Zinda or Mir Dastgir): A famous Sufi scholar, poet and preacher, born in 1314 CE in Herat, present-day Afghanistan. He traveled extensively throughout Central Asia, Iran and Anatolia, spreading the teachings of Sufism and establishing various Sufi orders. He is known for his poetry, especially ghazals and qasidas, and is considered one of the greatest figures in Chagatai literature. He was also a prolific writer and composed numerous works on Sufi philosophy and spirituality.
